supplementaryFacilitySource.title: General description of the PACTEL test facility, VTT Research Notes 1929
supplementaryFacilitySource.facts: Section 2.2.4 independently gives the 8.8 m height, 139.7 mm inner diameter and 7.77 m surge line with 27.3 mm inner diameter. Table A.3 (PDF page 85, printed A50) lists 133.5 litres pressurizer volume and 153.3 cm² flow area. The ideal cylindrical volume used by the IA-0231 input is 134.8854 litres; do not silently replace one with the other.

experiment.facility: PACTEL, Lappeenranta University of Technology, Finland
experiment.type: Separate-effects pressurizer insurge followed by outsurge
experiment.independence: Different facility, date and experiment from the Krško 2005 operating-plant transient. No PACTEL pressure samples may be used to calibrate model coefficients.
experiment.developmentUse: The report's mechanistic discussion informs model development. This is an independent event comparison, not a blind validation holdout. Fix parameters from cited dimensions, properties and correlations before the first comparison; do not tune them automatically to this pressure trace.
experiment.timeConvention: The experiment starts at t=0. Use the printed times unchanged; do not shift the curve to align its peak with a boundary event.
experiment.originalAcquisitionPeriodNote: The source does not state the measurement acquisition interval. Its 0.5 s output interval refers to TRACE graphics output, not measurement acquisition.

operatorEvents.event: Insurge stops; draining starts; facility core power switched off

experiment.operatorEventBasis: Table 2, printed page 7, PDF page 11. Core power maintains the external facility water temperature and is not a direct pressurizer heater input.

extraction.method: Decode the sole embedded RGB image on PDF page 17 using pypdf; retain only the red Pactel measurement path below the legend, reject black dashed TRACE pixels, and linearly resample the per-column median red-path height.
extraction.redSelection: R>=240 and R-G>=50 and R-B>=50; plot rows 130..634 exclude the legend. Multiple disjoint red branches in a column are rejected.
extraction.resamplingNote: The 1 s grid is a reading grid, not the unknown instrument acquisition grid. Six decimal places support byte reproducibility, not measurement precision.
extraction.allowanceBasis: A conservative two-pixel allowance in each axis. It is a graphical extraction allowance, not a stochastic instrument uncertainty. Boundary timing and digitization error are kept distinct.
extraction.endpointPolicy: Discard 0-4 s and 496-500 s; no extrapolation or invented endpoint measurements.

measuredInitialConditions.basis: Table 1, printed page 6, PDF page 10; geometry in section 2.2 and Figure 2.

publishedBoundaryModel.classification: Numeric boundary approximation from the report's TRACE input appendix; these are not raw instrument histories.
publishedBoundaryModel.basis: Appendix A-3/A-4 (PDF pages 28/29) and A-8/A-9 (PDF pages 33/34). Section 3 states the outsurge is the measured average flow, rather than a fitted discharge-orifice result.
publishedBoundaryModel.interpolation: Piecewise linear between published knots; hold the terminal value after the final knot.
publishedBoundaryModel.surgeSignConvention: Positive enters the pressurizer through its liquid region; negative removes liquid. Incoming enthalpy must not be used for outgoing liquid.
publishedBoundaryModel.inletTemperatureBasis: FILL tlin, Appendix A-3. Nearly saturated injection is described in section 2.2.1; the exact 547 K is a published calculation input, not an independently tabulated instrument measurement.
publishedBoundaryModel.temperatureBasis: Liquid/vapor initialization in Appendix A-3; wall initialization in A-7. These are TRACE setup values, not additional measured response channels.
publishedBoundaryModel.wallDimensionsBasis: Figure 2 gives pipe OD 168.3 mm and thickness 14.3 mm; Appendix A-7 gives inner/outer radii explicitly.
publishedBoundaryModel.wallMaterialBasis: Figure 2 parts list identifies vessel pipe item 1 as AISI 304 (heaters item 2 are AISI 316L). TRACE MATRD=6 appears in Appendix A-7. The report does not tabulate density, conductivity or heat-capacity functions; a surrogate must declare its own documented assumptions for them.
publishedBoundaryModel.heatLossBasis: Section 3.1 says 3.44 W/(m²K) was evaluated from facility heat loss; Appendix A-6 applies 3.44 and 298 K at the outer wall. The prose rounds ambient temperature to 25°C.

measurementUncertainty.basis: Section 4.1, printed page 13/PDF page 16, gives the maximum pressure-measurement error for this test and states it also applies to the other tests.
measurementUncertainty.distribution: Unspecified. Treat as a reported error bound, not one standard deviation.
measurementUncertainty.conditionalEnvelopeBasis: Arithmetic sum of the reported 0.094 MPa pressure error bound and the separate 0.0142857 MPa two-pixel reading allowance. Apply the separate ±1.20048 s graphical time allowance when reporting conditional coverage. This is not a statistical confidence interval or a complete uncertainty budget.
measurementUncertainty.flowNote: The ±0.000793 kg/s spray-flow error in section 4.6 belongs to ATWS-21. It must not be transferred to the ATWS-10 insurge or outsurge.

calibrationAndHoldout.parameterFitting: No pressure response values calibrate geometry, wall heat capacity, heat-transfer coefficients, phase transfer, mixing, or timing. Do not optimize against this curve.
calibrationAndHoldout.acceptance: This is a conditional component comparison. Report raw discrepancies and the separately stated measurement/reading bounds. Unknown input and model uncertainties prevent a blanket plant-validation pass.

limitations: PACTEL is a small pressurizer experiment for a volume-scaled VVER-440 facility, not a 1000 MWe PWR operating-plant transient. It tests pressure physics and does not validate the coupled power plant.
Measured pressure is a digitized figure rather than the original acquisition dataset; no calibration file or original measurement timestamps are supplied.

The 491 resampled positions are correlated readings along one plotted curve, not 491 independent raw instrument samples. Coverage percentages and RMSE are descriptive comparisons, not confidence levels.
Flow and temperature forcing uses the published study's boundary approximation. Continuous measured flow, inlet temperature and heater electrical-power histories are unavailable in the report.
Only pressure is held out. Wall/fluid temperature and level response curves are not supplied by this report for independent scoring.
The Table 1 pressure 5.9 MPa and Figure 5 pre-event trace near 5.86 MPa differ slightly; both are preserved without offset correction.
Figure 5 reaches its measured peak near 219 s, while Table 2 stops insurge at 221 s. No time shift or boundary timing adjustment is made to hide this difference.
The reported wall heat-loss coefficient is a facility estimate; its uncertainty and temperature dependence are not specified.
A lumped implementation omits the published surge-line inventory, hydrostatic distribution and axial/radial wall temperature fields unless those effects are modeled explicitly.

The chosen cylindrical geometry follows IA-0231's published benchmark input. The independent facility description lists 133.5 litres rather than the ideal cylinder's 134.885 litres; actual surge-line geometry also differs from the simplified input. This geometry approximation is preserved and disclosed rather than fitted to pressure.
The report's general text describes injection after 100 s; the case-specific measured operator table and published boundary table put ATWS-10 insurge at 120 s. Use the case-specific times.

conclusion: The independent PACTEL component comparison executed. Its descriptive pressure envelope covers 343 of 491 correlated digitized positions. This is not a blind holdout, a statistical confidence result, or a plant-validation pass. All raw discrepancies and numerical balance checks are retained.

numericalEvidence.candidateSelection: 48×8 was selected as the finest tested mesh, with shrinking axial differences, before measured scoring. Residual spatial error remains unresolved; no asymptotic or grid-convergence-index claim.

experiment.facility: PACTEL, Lappeenranta University of Technology, Finland

operatorEvents.event: Insurge stops; draining starts (outside selected window)

experiment.windowReason: ATWS-11's outsurge mass-flow magnitude is not published in the tables or printed input decks. The comparison stops before draining rather than inferring the missing boundary from pressure.
experiment.independence: Different experiment from ATWS-10, in the same facility and publication. ATWS-11 pressure is withheld from the model developer until a candidate hash freeze for this development cycle.
experiment.qualification: The report's general mechanisms were already available during development; this is a development-separated response holdout, not historically blind external validation or certification.

extraction.method: Decode the sole embedded RGB image on PDF page 18; retain only the red Pactel measurement path below the legend and only columns needed by the prespecified pre-drain window. Linearly resample median path height between adjacent represented pixel columns.
extraction.redSelection: R>=240 and R-G>=50 and R-B>=50. Rows 120..614 exclude the legend. Disjoint red branches in a required column are rejected.
extraction.readingGridQualification: 291 correlated positions along a published curve, not 291 independent instrument acquisitions. Six decimals preserve reproducibility, not measurement precision.
extraction.endpointPolicy: No extrapolation. Discard 0-4 s; no values after 295 s enter this reference. The time allowance is clipped at the available reference-window edges.

publishedBoundaryModel.classification: Conditional replay combining ATWS-11 table values with explicitly inherited ATWS-10 input-deck approximations; not a complete raw measured input record.
publishedBoundaryModel.geometryAndWallParameters: Shared unchanged with the frozen PactelPressurizer model: 8.8 m height, 0.1397 m inner diameter, 0.0143 m wall, 3.44 W/(m2 K) exterior coefficient, 298 K ambient. Constitutive assumptions are separately recorded by the model.
publishedBoundaryModel.forcingQualification: One-second ramps and 547 K inlet/wall conditions follow the printed ATWS-10 input pattern; they are not additional ATWS-11 measurements. Fluid temperatures correspond to the same 5.9 MPa initial pressure. No input is recovered from pressure response.

measurementUncertainty.basis: Section 4.1 printed page 13/PDF page 16 states this maximum pressure-measurement error also applies to the other experiments in the report.
measurementUncertainty.distribution: Unspecified; this is a reported bound, not a standard deviation.
measurementUncertainty.conditionalEnvelopeBasis: Arithmetic sum of 0.094 MPa reported pressure bound and 0.0142857 MPa graphical allowance, combined with a separate ±1.440576 s graphical-time window. Not a confidence interval or complete uncertainty budget.

calibrationAndHoldout.parameterFitting: No ATWS-11 pressure value may select coefficients, wall properties, mesh, initial conditions, boundary timing, offsets, or the model revision.
calibrationAndHoldout.acceptance: Report raw discrepancies and descriptive conditional-envelope coverage separately from numerical checks. No whole-plant validation pass is inferred.

limitations: This is a PACTEL component experiment, not a 1000 MWe PWR operating-plant transient or operator-training qualification.

The model developer was kept separate from ATWS-11 response values during this development cycle, but the same publication's general discussion was already known. This is not an externally certified blind study.
Only the compression phase is scored. ATWS-11 outsurge magnitude is unavailable and has not been invented; the subsequent expansion response is not validated.
The 1 s extraction grid samples a plotted curve; positions are correlated and original acquisition timestamps/calibration data are unavailable.
Boundary ramp duration, inlet temperature and initial wall/fluid temperatures partly reuse ATWS-10 assumptions. Their ATWS-11 uncertainties are not documented.
The conditional pressure envelope is incomplete because input, geometry and model uncertainties are not fully characterized.
No pressure offset correction or time alignment is applied, including any mismatch between the measured initial table and plotted curve.
A successful numerical balance does not establish agreement with measurements, and the held-out event cannot establish full-plant fidelity.

candidateFreeze.scope: The ATWS-11 pressure response was withheld from this model-development cycle. The source report general discussion was already available. This is not historically blind external validation.

supersedes.reason: Independent pre-release audit found that native auxiliary-feedwater automatic demand did not latch when initialized below its low-level threshold. This unrelated plant-system initialization defect is corrected before scoring the reserved pressure response.
supersedes.qualification: Pre-scoring candidate replacement; no ATWS-11 candidate discrepancies had been computed or used. Original freeze and source are preserved.

protocol.selectionBasis: Initial conditions and operator-event input completeness in NUREG/IA-0231 Tables 1 and 2, before extracting or evaluating the ATWS-11 measured pressure response.
protocol.windowReason: The published outsurge mass flow is not tabulated for ATWS-11. Stop two seconds before the Table 2 draining event at 297 s; do not infer outflow from pressure or extend the comparison through an unidentified boundary.

forcing.interpolation: Piecewise linear between knots; hold the terminal value only within the declared simulation window.

inputQualifications: 5.9 MPa, 3.5 m and 0.217 kg/s are the rounded measured initial/input values in Table 1.
Heater shutdown at 100 s and insurge initiation at 119 s are Table 2 operator events.
The one-second boundary ramps are a declared approximation following the ATWS-10 appendix input convention. ATWS-11's actual high-frequency flow ramp is unavailable.

The ATWS-10 appendix supplies 547 K inlet/wall and 547.64 K fluid temperatures. ATWS-11 has the same initial pressure; reusing these thermal initial/boundary assumptions is explicit, not an additional measured ATWS-11 temperature record.
The vessel geometry, material and exterior-loss assumptions are shared unchanged with the fixed candidate model. No held-out pressure point may set them.
The facility's 245 kW core power maintains external loop conditions and is not deposited directly into the pressurizer.

numericalProtocol.spatialConvergence: Use the model configuration frozen before unblinding. Do not select a mesh by held-out response error.

scoring.graphicalAllowance: Two pixels in each axis, determined from reviewed Figure 6 axis calibration independently of model results.
scoring.timeAlignment: None; retain printed times and operator events.
scoring.offsetCorrection: None; retain any mismatch between Table 1 initialization and Figure 6 pressure.
scoring.acceptance: No blanket physical-validation pass. Report conditional envelope coverage descriptively and separately from numerical acceptance.

developmentSeparation.rule: Record candidate model, wrapper, runner and comparator hashes before computing held-out errors. A later model change invalidates the original holdout claim; retain prior results and label subsequent evaluations as post-unblinding.
developmentSeparation.qualification: Same-facility independent experiment with response withheld from this development cycle. The source report's general discussion was already available; this is not a historically blind external certification study.

assumptions: This is a PACTEL component experiment, not a 1000 MWe PWR operating-plant transient or operator-training qualification.

The model developer was kept separate from ATWS-11 response values during this development cycle, but the same publication's general discussion was already known. This is not an externally certified blind study.
Only the compression phase is scored. ATWS-11 outsurge magnitude is unavailable and has not been invented; the subsequent expansion response is not validated.
The 1 s extraction grid samples a plotted curve; positions are correlated and original acquisition timestamps/calibration data are unavailable.
Boundary ramp duration, inlet temperature and initial wall/fluid temperatures partly reuse ATWS-10 assumptions. Their ATWS-11 uncertainties are not documented.
The conditional pressure envelope is incomplete because input, geometry and model uncertainties are not fully characterized.
No pressure offset correction or time alignment is applied, including any mismatch between the measured initial table and plotted curve.
A successful numerical balance does not establish agreement with measurements, and the held-out event cannot establish full-plant fidelity.
